title: Dedicated autoscaler: priority routing, burst controls, and utilization reporting enhancement
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally experience short high-concurrency spikes from customer traffic patterns (bursty inference loads). Current autoscaler reacts too slowly and does not account for request priority, which leads to degraded SLAs for high-priority customers during contention. This PR adds three coordinated improvements: (1) priority-aware routing in the dedicated autoscaler so higher-tier requests can borrow burst capacity, (2) token-bucket based burst controls with smoothing to avoid sudden aggressive scale-ups, and (3) improved utilization reporting and dashboards to make burst behavior visible to ops and customers.

Summary of changes: added a priority routing layer that tags requests with PriorityClass and routes allocation decisions in the fleet autoscaler; implemented a token-bucket smoothing layer that limits burst consumption and decays burst credits over configurable windows; instrumented detailed utilization metrics (per-fleet, per-priority, rolling percentiles, burst_credit usage) and added a console dashboard for these metrics; added flags and config schema to allow per-customer burst caps and per-fleet priority weights.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement priority routing algorithm and unit tests
- [x] Implement token-bucket burst controls with smoothing and tests
- [x] Add Prometheus metrics & dashboard JSON
- [x] Add e2e smoke-tests and canary rollout plan
- [x] Add Linear ticket and update release notes

Testing and validation: unit tests added for priority routing and token-bucket smoothing (pkg/autoscaler/*_test.go). Integration tests simulate multi-tenant traffic with mixed priorities; CI run showed a flaky integration test initially which was fixed by tightening the test harness timing (see commits). Benchmarks (perf lab) show median 95th latency improvement for priority requests under burst load: 15% reduction vs baseline and reduced tail latency spikes. Observability: new metrics prefixed dedicated_autoscaler_* and a dashboard (console/dashboards/dedicated_autoscaler_priority.json) were added for on-call.

Rollout plan: staged canary across three fleets with feature flag dedicated.autoscaler.priority_routing enabled. Start with internal fleets then opt-in customers. Default behavior remains unchanged unless the feature flag and per-fleet config are set. Config includes burst_capacity_per_minute, burst_decay_seconds, and priority_weights. Backwards compatibility: config defaults preserve previous autoscaler semantics.

Related: Linear ENG-4123 tracked design and testing. SUP-1543 captured customer report that motivated the priority routing work.

Notes: this change touches allocation hot paths; micro-optimizations were kept minimal to preserve readability. Priority routing adds a small constant overhead (measured ~1.2% CPU at baseline load).

Feature behind feature flag dedicated.autoscaler.priority_routing. See docs/release_notes/dedicated_autoscaler.md for config and rollout instructions.
